Expeditions

Bonaire Baseline Surveys

Mapping reefs through repeat field surveys

Explore the work

ProjectsResearchExpeditionsDiscuss a project

Location: Bonaire.

Survey years: 2023 and 2026.

Collaboration: STINAPA.

My role: custom survey equipment and methods; leadership of the 2026 survey campaign.

I designed underwater photogrammetry equipment and methods for repeat reef surveys in Bonaire. In 2026, I led a campaign across 18 sites, collecting imagery to build a detailed spatial record of the reefs.

The assignment

The fieldwork focused on collecting underwater images for reef mapping. It connected survey design and custom equipment with the practical work of documenting sites underwater.

The 2026 campaign

  • 18 reef sites surveyed.
  • 70,885 source images collected.
  • Approximately 34,160 m², or 3.42 hectares, of reef mapped.

After the dives

I built a Python and Agisoft Metashape pipeline to process imagery into 3D reconstructions, orthomosaics, and GIS exports, with checkpoints for measurements and review. I also built Deeptime, a prototype viewer for exploring large reef orthomosaics.

Working underwater

A camera operator captures overlapping passes from deeper to shallower reef contours. A second diver positions and retrieves scale bars, records reference depths, and helps establish the survey bounds. After capture, the images become inputs for reconstruction and mapping.

The 2026 campaign ran from 15 August to 4 October, around Bonaire and Klein Bonaire.

Follow the data

  • 2026 final report: survey summary, methods, and all 18 site reports.
  • Deeptime: processing and visualization.
